title: Back When You Called Us Devils
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High schooler Yusuke Saito has lost six months of memory, and people from his middle-school past begin confronting him with accusations that he and a friend tortured, maimed and sexually assaulted other children. The psychological thriller follows him as he uncovers what he did and faces the people he hurt.
life_message: A person must face the full truth of the harm they did before any atonement is possible.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Victims seek personal reckoning (AniList Revenge) rather than going to authorities, who missed the crimes (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Unchecked teens did harm; the story favours accountability over license.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Focus on the individual and his victims; family barely noticed (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Teachers and parents fail; authority not trusted.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Moral reckoning framed psychologically, not religiously (to verify).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Characters fight for safety and survival against past threats.

folkways.japan: School bullying (ijime) unnoticed by teachers reflects a recurring Japanese social concern, here used as the root of the crimes.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer says volume 1 raises discomfiting questions more than answers (ANN); MU lists Atonement and Redemption.
delivery.note: The question of whether a changed person can atone is carried by the mystery rather than stated outright (to verify past volume 1).

winners_losers: Victims seek reckoning and the protagonist must face what he was; sympathy is divided and the worldview of atonement through confrontation is favoured (to verify ending).
